section_summary: This section begins with estimates of Japan’s merchant shipping and then addresses the seizure, use, restitution, and postwar allocation of Japanese and former Allied vessels. It includes Swedish claims for the S/S Miramar, proposals for transferring title to captured Japanese ships, rules for returning Allied craft, British and American exchanges over merchant fleet reparations, and a restitution request concerning the S.S. Islas Visayas.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum transmitting JS-34 addenda
subfiles.from: Constance G. Gaynor, Foreign Economic Administration
subfiles.to: J. W. Ballantine, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits addenda on the volume and character of Japan’s merchant shipping.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a copy of the JS-34 addenda.

subfiles.title: Addenda to The Volume and Character of Japan’s Merchant Shipping
subfiles.about: Explains estimates of Japanese shipping employment, cargo tonnage, and bulk carrying capacity.
subfiles.summary: The addenda describe sources and methods for estimating where Japanese commercial ships operated in 1937–38, including overseas, coastal, and nearseas service. They also explain cargo tonnage conversions and the Joint Target Group’s calculation of annual bulk carrying capacity from vessel size, speed, routes, port time, and operating days.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Captured Japanese Merchant Vessels
subfiles.about: Reports approval of a procedure for divesting Japanese interests in merchant vessels.
subfiles.summary: Requests a peace treaty provision ratifying transfers of Japanese vessel interests.

subfiles.title: J.C.S. 1500/3: Disposition of Captured Japanese Merchant Vessels
subfiles.doc_type: committee report with appendices and annex
subfiles.from: Joint Logistics Committee and Joint Military Transportation Committee
subfiles.about: Recommends requisition and transfer of Japanese vessel titles, backed by a peace treaty and selective prize proceedings.
subfiles.summary: The report compares prize proceedings, Japanese government requisition, and a peace treaty as means of removing Japanese ownership interests. It recommends that the Japanese government requisition vessels selected by SCAP and transfer the interests to SCAP on behalf of the United Nations, with treaty ratification and prize cases where ownership is uncertain. Its appendices contain draft instructions, legal analysis, and a Marianas naval speedletter supporting requisition as the faster method.

subfiles.title: Swedish memorandum concerning S/S Miramar
subfiles.about: Requests release of the Swedish S/S Miramar from Japanese control.
subfiles.summary: The Legation recounts the Miramar’s Japanese seizure at Saigon and subsequent charter under protest to avoid outright confiscation. It argues that Japanese naval use and the coerced charter did not make the Swedish ship Japanese property, and asks U.S. authorities to return it to its owners. Pages 19–22 contain overlapping copies of the memorandum.

subfiles.title: Brief History of Seizure and Charter of S/S Miramar
subfiles.about: Chronicles the Miramar’s charter, seizure, protests, movements, and later Japanese charter.
subfiles.summary: The chronology runs from its 1940 charter through its seizure in December 1941, detention of officers, Swedish protests, a November 1942 bareboat charter, and the last charter payment in 1944.

subfiles.title: Reply on the S/S Miramar
subfiles.about: Advises that the Miramar’s status is under investigation.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further reply after requested information is received.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese whaling ships
subfiles.about: Seeks the location, condition, and potential availability for purchase of Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: Carpenter writes for a Norwegian interested in buying surviving Japanese factory ships. The enclosures ask which ships survive, where they are, their condition, and who controls sales; a list identifies six vessels and notes that their fate is uncertain.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on Japanese whaling ships
subfiles.about: Requests a prompt answer to the December inquiry about Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: Carpenter follows up before his Norwegian contact leaves New York.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Japanese whaling factories
subfiles.about: Provides limited information on the fate and disposition of Japanese whaling ships.
subfiles.summary: Four listed ships were reportedly sunk; the fate of two and the disposition of survivors remain unknown.

subfiles.title: Swedish memorandum enclosing protests over S/S Miramar
subfiles.about: Submits the Swedish Minister’s 1942 protests concerning Japanese seizure of the Miramar.
subfiles.summary: Emphasizes that any Japanese use of the Miramar occurred against Sweden’s strong objection.

subfiles.title: First Swedish protest over S/S Miramar
subfiles.from: W. Bagge, Swedish Minister in Tokyo
subfiles.to: Shigenori Togo, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Protests the seizure of the Miramar and coercion of its officers.
subfiles.summary: Bagge reports Japanese naval seizure at Saigon, forced service by Swedish officers, and interference with neutral Swedish property and navigation. He requests the ship’s immediate release.

subfiles.title: Second Swedish protest over S/S Miramar
subfiles.from: W. Bagge, Swedish Minister in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Renews Sweden’s demand for release of the Miramar after the first protest went unanswered.
subfiles.summary: Bagge protests continued Japanese use of the vessel and asks for its return to Swedish owners.

subfiles.title: Proposed telegram on division of Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.about: Seeks Soviet agreement to delay division of certain Japanese warships until surrender duties end.
subfiles.summary: The proposed message says Japanese submarines and larger combatants will be destroyed, while destroyers and smaller surface combatants will be divided equally among four powers after their repatriation and minesweeping work is finished.

subfiles.title: Transmission of policy on release of former Allied vessels
subfiles.about: Forwards U.S. policy and a directive on releasing former Allied vessels captured by Japan.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed policy lets SCAP use recaptured Allied craft, return public vessels and craft under 500 gross tons to claimant nations, and use the Combined Shipping Adjustment Board for larger merchant and private craft.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum on release of former Allied vessels
subfiles.from: John A. Hilldring, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Requests circulation of approved vessel-release conclusions and directive to Far Eastern Commission members.
subfiles.summary: Reports Joint Chiefs’ concurrence and dispatch of the directive to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Decision on SWNCC 227/8
subfiles.about: Records approval of arrangements for releasing former Allied vessels captured by Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that SWNCC 227/8 was approved by informal action.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 227/8: Arrangements for Release to Claimant Nations
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for SCAP to use and release captured former Allied vessels and waterborne craft.
subfiles.summary: The report recommends that SCAP retain former Allied vessels while needed for occupation, repatriation, and Japan’s minimum economy. SCAP may return public vessels and craft under 500 gross tons directly where title is clear; the Combined Shipping Adjustment Board is to handle larger merchant and private craft and protect against liability. Appendices supply background, reasoning, a proposed memorandum to the Joint Chiefs, and a draft directive. Several pages are duplicate impressions of the same text.

subfiles.title: Corrigendum to SWNCC 227/8
subfiles.about: Directs replacement of a revised page in the vessel-release report.
subfiles.summary: Requests substitution of revised page 38 and destruction of the old page.

subfiles.title: Conversation on division of the Japanese fleet
subfiles.about: Records British questions about allocation of Japan’s naval and merchant fleets.
subfiles.summary: Graves argues that countries beyond the Far Eastern Commission should receive Japanese merchant shipping and that losses in both European and Far Eastern wars should count. Vincent distinguishes naval division from merchant reparations and says the claims question will be studied.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire on Japanese merchant and fishing fleets
subfiles.about: Seeks assurance that merchant fleet claims are distinct from the four-way division of naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Britain supports consideration of claims from Norway and other countries outside the Far Eastern Commission and accepts an Allied reparations body operating under Commission policies.

subfiles.title: Conversation on principles for dividing Japanese merchant and fishing fleets
subfiles.about: Records British advocacy of the German shipping allocation formula for Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Graves proposes shares proportional to overall wartime shipping losses. Vincent questions the statistical effect and says the earlier German settlement did not necessarily establish a Japanese precedent.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Reports preparation of a U.S. reply and discusses eligible claims and wartime loss calculations.
subfiles.summary: States that countries at war with Japan or damaged by that war may claim ships.

subfiles.title: U.S. reply to British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Confirms separate treatment of naval vessels and merchant and fishing fleet reparations.
subfiles.summary: The reply supports allocation through an Allied reparations commission under Far Eastern Commission policies and consideration of shipping losses caused by Japan for all countries that fought it.

subfiles.title: Second filed copy of conversation on division principles
subfiles.about: Duplicates the conversation on Britain’s proposed allocation formula for Japanese merchant ships.
subfiles.summary: Graves favors gross-tonnage shares based on losses in both wars; Vincent reserves the U.S. position.

subfiles.title: British views on reparations from Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. reservation against treating the German shipping formula as precedent for Japanese reparations.
subfiles.summary: Attaches a draft reply and cites the American reservation recorded at the Inter-Allied Reparations Agency.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japanese whaling operations in the Antarctic
subfiles.about: Records British objections to proposed Japanese Antarctic whaling under SCAP permission.
subfiles.summary: Graves opposes Japanese whaling and asks about whale-oil allocation; Vincent cites Japan’s food needs and whaling rules.

subfiles.title: Request for comments on British fleet and whaling representations
subfiles.about: Requests comments and a basis for answering British questions on merchant ships and whaling.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a proposed reply before a further conversation with Graves.

subfiles.title: Second filed copy of conversation on Japanese fleet division
subfiles.about: Duplicates the August conversation on naval and merchant fleet allocation.
subfiles.summary: Graves raises wider national claims and overall war losses; Vincent says merchant disposition depends on reparations decisions.

subfiles.title: Second filed copy of British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Duplicates Britain’s request for inclusive merchant and fishing fleet reparations procedures.
subfiles.summary: Distinguishes naval allocation and urges consideration of nonmember countries’ merchant shipping losses.

subfiles.title: British memorandum proposing division principles
subfiles.about: Proposes applying the German merchant shipping allocation principles to Japanese tonnage.
subfiles.summary: Britain recommends allocation by gross tonnage lost in both wars, with attention to ships’ quality, age, and type, and asks whether the United States agrees.

subfiles.title: U.S. response to British allocation proposal
subfiles.about: Reserves the U.S. position on using the German shipping formula for Japanese reparations.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it has not decided the issue and recalls its explicit reservation that the German arrangement established no precedent for Japanese shipping.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese merchant marine study
subfiles.to: Acting United States Representative to the United Nations
subfiles.about: Sends a declassified study for Far East reconstruction work.
subfiles.summary: Requests delivery of the study to Adrien H. Alcan at Lake Success.

subfiles.title: Restitution of S.S. Islas Visayas
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests that Panama submit a formal restitution claim for the Islas Visayas.
subfiles.summary: Lists vessel description, ownership proof, and seizure circumstances needed for the claim.

subfiles.title: Note to Panama concerning S.S. Islas Visayas
subfiles.about: Asks Panama, as the vessel’s flag state, to file a formal restitution claim.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes the requested evidence and explains that British owners may help Panama document the claim for return of the vessel.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to British Embassy concerning S.S. Islas Visayas
subfiles.about: Advises Britain of the Panamanian restitution claim request for the British-owned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on the ship’s description, title, and Japanese acquisition; the text continues beyond page 80.
